A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeCo study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original WarpBench/OccluBench experiments, estimator robustness tests, video-model benchmarking, and GeCo-guided generation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds geometric-baseline results and a real-versus-generated video comparison.

M1.justification: The motion/depth computation, scale-invariant fusion, temporal aggregation, and inference guidance procedure are unchanged. The appendix implementation and optimization schedules are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets, static-scene tasks, and generation scenarios. The new real-versus-generated analysis samples existing DL3DV and GeCo-Eval coverage; it introduces no new domain or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands the quantitative baseline comparison beyond MEt3R by adding WorldScore and TSED. Table 3 adds WorldScore for deformation and occlusion localization; TSED is explicitly excluded from dense localization. New Table 6 compares all three baselines with GeCo, substantially broadening evaluated geometric comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds a protocol comparing 30 real and 30 generated videos, with five generated clips per model and reported comparable motion magnitudes. Existing benchmark sizes, preprocessing, evaluation windows, and guidance settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 6 examines whether metrics assign greater consistency to real videos than generated videos with comparable motion. This extends metric-validity analysis. Existing component studies, noise sensitivity tests, motion analyses, and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: V3 introduces Cohen's d standardized effect sizes for the real-versus-generated comparison. Existing four-seed generation and seed-42 sampling disclosures remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: Comparative results expand substantially: Table 2 adds WorldScore detection accuracies of 32.95%/81.54% and TSED accuracies of 36.78%/38.46% on CO3D-Warp/ScanNet-Warp, and Table 3 adds WorldScore localization results. New Table 6 reports d values of +0.349 for GeCo, +0.354 for WorldScore, +0.322 for TSED, and -0.361 for MEt3R. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The metric equations, geometric assumptions, guidance objective, and appendix derivations are unchanged. Cohen's d is introduced as an empirical statistic without a new mathematical derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly claims that GeCo supports finetuning and distillation through differentiability, without corresponding experiments. The central claims about joint artifact detection, benchmarking, and training-free guidance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations of WorldScore's scene-versus-object performance and TSED's sparse coverage. It interprets MEt3R's negative real/generated effect size through semantic-feature sensitivity and states that valid metrics should not systematically favor generated videos. Existing rigidity, runtime, and estimator limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The supplementary introduction removes the instruction to consult the attached video_results.html file. This changes documented access information without establishing that the resource itself disappeared. The project URL, hardware, backbone specifications, and appendix hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Figure 1 revises prior-work attribution: its WorldScore-labeled illustration and associated occlusion-detection description become a depth-cue illustration. This locally changes WorldScore's portrayal. The reference list, related-work taxonomy, and overall novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract and introductory wording, adds experimental discussion and acknowledgements, and preserves the section structure. Editing is limited rather than comprehensive; Section 4.1 also introduces a duplicated sentence about WorldScore and TSED.

P2.justification: V3 expands Tables 2–3 and adds Table 6, renumbering the guidance table to 7. Figures 5–6 exchange numbering and placement, Figure 1 changes labels, and Figure 9 rearranges the existing globe/dog examples horizontally. Other figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The geometric-baseline comparisons in Tables 2–3 strengthen validation beyond the earlier MEt3R comparison, while new Table 6 supplies a useful motion-comparable metric check. Figure 1's revised attribution also resolves conflicting descriptions of WorldScore. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new comparison, duplicated prose, and the untested finetuning/distillation claim; the method and established results remain unchanged.
